author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page
summary: A read-only specialty directory answering the inverse of the veterinarian directory: which veterinarians hold each specialty. Lists every specialty by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it
each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
a veterinarian who holds no specialty is not listed, because the page is organised by specialty and lists specialties rather than the full veterinarian roster
a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians shown under it
all specialties render on a single page with no pagination
specialties, and the veterinarians within each specialty, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
notes: Inverse view of the existing Veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001); reuses the existing Vet/Specialty model and seeded data. Route /specialties.html and view naming are best-effort; system-design-expert may revise. Full name follows the vetList convention of first name then last name.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the inverse of the vet directory and reuses the established vet-feature patterns unchanged: a Spring Data repository interface, a server-rendered @Controller returning a Thymeleaf template, all in the existing org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet package (system-design.md#package-structure, #contracts). The one adjustment — the reason this is minor not covered — is how the inverse view reaches data. The vet_specialties @ManyToMany is unidirectional: Vet owns it (vet/Vet.java:47-50) and Specialty (vet/Specialty.java) has no back-reference, so the mapping cannot be navigated from the specialty side. The directory is therefore assembled in the controller by inverting the existing Vet.getSpecialties() associations. Verified by Read of vet/Vet.java, vet/Specialty.java, owner/PetTypeRepository.java, and templates/vets/vetList.html; IntelliJ oracle not connected on this run, so these are Read-backed resolution claims rather than search_symbol-cited.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html on SpecialtyController, returning view specialties/specialtyList — mirrors VetController.showVetList but with no pagination (single page, per acceptance criteria).

SpecialtyController injects the existing VetRepository (for the cached findAll() carrying each vet's eager specialties) plus the new SpecialtyRepository (authoritative complete specialty list). No change to VetController or VetRepository.
New Thymeleaf template under templates/specialties/ using the shared fragments/layout, iterating specialties then the vets under each — structural mirror of vetList.html minus the pagination block.

Any new #{...} message key the template introduces (for example a page heading) MUST be added to every one of the eleven messages_*.properties bundles, or the REQ-LANG-002 build-time language-parity test fails.

patterns.description: Name-ordered lookup query (@Query ... ORDER BY name) — the exact precedent for SpecialtyRepository returning all specialties in name order. SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty,Integer> (or JpaRepository) with e.g. List<Specialty> findSpecialties() ordered by name.
Server-rendered @Controller / @GetMapping returning a template view name — the shape SpecialtyController copies, dropping the Pageable/pagination helpers.

Vet.getSpecialties() already returns specialties sorted by name; the inverse grouping reads this collection per vet. Group by specialty NAME (Specialty extends NamedEntity) so grouping does not depend on entity equals/id semantics.
@WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean(MockMvc is the one sanctioned mock) controller-test pattern to clone for SpecialtyControllerTests; mock both SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository.

risks.risk: Deriving the specialty list from the vets (grouping vets by their specialties) would silently drop a specialty held by no veterinarian — violating acceptance edge 1. The H2 seed data (db/h2/data.sql: radiology, surgery, dentistry all held) contains no orphan specialty, so this defect would pass the seeded app and only surface later.
risks.mitigation: Make SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() the authoritative, name-ordered source of the specialty list; seed the view with an entry for every specialty (empty vet list allowed), then fill vets by inverting VetRepository.findAll(). The theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtiesHeldByNoVeterinarian test must construct an orphan specialty via the mocked SpecialtyRepository since the seed data has none.

risks.risk: Passing a raw Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> or Map<String,Object> to the template breaches the typed-interface principle (architecture-principles.md checklist: no raw Map for data transfer).
risks.mitigation: Introduce a small package-private view record in the vet package (e.g. record SpecialtyListing(String name, List<String> veterinarians)) carrying the specialty name and the ordered full-name strings; the controller builds the List<SpecialtyListing> and the template stays dumb.

Specialties in name order (from the repository query). Vets within each specialty in a deterministic order — last name then first name — with the display string formatted first-name-space-last-name to match the vetList.html convention (vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName).

notes: Both product-flagged edges CONFIRMED, not rejected. Edge 1 (specialty held by no veterinarian still listed) is load-bearing: it is precisely why the specialty list must come from SpecialtyRepository rather than from grouping vets. Edge 2 (stable ordering) CONFIRMED: specialties by name (mirrors PetTypeRepository and Vet.getSpecialties), vets by last-then-first name. Verdict is minor (not new): no new module, pattern, or integration — every building block already exists in the vet/owner packages; the only genuine design choice is the controller-side inversion plus the orphan-safe specialty source. No ADR: nothing hard-to-reverse or trade-off-bearing. No system-design.md edit made now — the architectural patterns are unchanged and the doc records current state; doc-sync should add SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository rows to the Contracts table and wire REQ-SPEC-001 into their Implements column after the code lands. Route /specialties.html and view name specialties/specialtyList are best-effort per the prd-entry and adopted as-is. The page is not required in the top nav (REQ-SYS-001 scopes nav to owner + vet areas); the layout fragment call needs a menu selector — reuse 'vets' or pass an inert value, a template detail, not a blocker. NG-2 (no managing vets/specialties) is respected: this slice is read-only, GET-only.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: all user-derived values (specialty.name, veterinarian full names) render via th:text (HTML-escaped) with no th:utext; mirrors the existing vetList.html pattern, so no XSS.
SQL/JPQL: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static parameterless JPQL query with no concatenation; no injection surface.

New public GET /specialties.html endpoint exposes no new data class - vet and specialty names are already public via the existing vet directory, consistent with the app-wide no-auth model (no spring-security config present).
Read-only, GET-only slice honoring NG-2: no write path, no deserialization, no file I/O, no secrets, no new dependency.
Non-paginated result set is a product decision over admin-seeded data; DOS is out of scope and no user-controlled input reaches the query or template.

findings.description: Column 1 header uses #{specialties} (renders "Specialties") as the label for the specialty-name column. Human sign-off is needed: accept the plural label as-is, or absorb the i18n parity churn to introduce a #{specialty} singular key.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test-review skill checklist opens with "Per the brief (§ Mocking Policy), this project allows no mock libraries at all" and lists "No Mockito, EasyMock, or any mock/stub library usage" as a required check. Both docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy and CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy say Mockito is "tolerated, not encouraged" and that new tests should reach for real implementations or hand-written doubles first — not that Mockito is prohibited. The skill summary overstates the restriction: it would mis-flag every @WebMvcTest controller test in the project (including the existing VetControllerTests that this slice explicitly clones). A human decision is needed: either update the skill checklist to reflect the brief ("tolerated, not encouraged; conscious exception") or tighten the brief to prohibit Mockito outright and add explicit guidance for the orphan-specialty class of test where real fixtures would require seeding a separate test DB.

approved_aspects: All five PRD test_names (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtiesHeldByNoVeterinarian, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage) are present and each assertion would fail on a genuine regression of the named behavior
AssertJ containsExactly used for both specialty ordering (alphabetical) and vet ordering within specialty (last-then-first), directly verifying the stable-order acceptance criterion
doesNotContain and isEmpty() correctly verify omission of vet-with-no-specialty and the empty-vet-list for orphan specialty respectively
Factory methods specialty() and vet() wrap all domain object construction — no raw constructor calls in test bodies
BDD naming convention (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) followed on all five methods
Four-phase structure maintained: @BeforeEach arranges, per-test perform() acts, assertThat/andExpect asserts, no cleanup needed

@MockitoBean on SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository is a conscious exception justified by: (a) the orphan-specialty edge case is not present in H2 seed data and cannot be exercised without either a mock or additional test-fixture DB setup, (b) the design-block explicitly instructs this pattern, (c) it mirrors the established VetControllerTests shape, and (d) the brief explicitly says mock-framework stubs are tolerated
The no-pagination test explicitly asserts totalPages/currentPage/totalItems attributes are absent from the model, making the single-page constraint machine-verifiable rather than inferred
Hamcrest hasSize via MockMvc model().attribute() fluent chain is the standard Spring MVC test DSL integration point, not a raw JUnit assertion violation
Straight-line test bodies with no branching or loops
Setup comments explain test-data semantics (why dentistry is the orphan, why Douglas precedes Leary) at a level not derivable from the code alone — these are scenario annotations, not narration
